      CGB.SelfProduction.renewableActionWorld CGB.RenewableLearning.Env.feedB 0 CGB.RenewableLearning.Env.missB = 1
doc: In the same certified world, aligned ready bodies have two equally likely next-world states while their next body state is the same. The current sensory labels of those world states coincide, yet a subsequent action 0 distinguishes them by the world's next `missB` probability. This is a conditional one-step world-law statement, not a claim of infinite entropy or learned prediction.

name: CGB.SelfProduction.repeated_assimilation_association_readout
signature:
∀ {dv dk : ℕ} (precision : ℕ → Fin dk → ℝ) (natural : ℕ → Fin dv → Fin dk → ℝ) (p₀ w query : Fin dk → ℝ)
  (m₀ target : Fin dv → Fin dk → ℝ),
  (∀ (j : Fin dk), 0 < p₀ j) →
    (∀ (j : Fin dk), 0 ≤ w j) →
      (∀ (j : Fin dk), precision 0 j = p₀ j) →
        (∀ (i : Fin dv) (j : Fin dk), natural 0 i j = p₀ j * m₀ i j) →
          (∀ (n : ℕ) (j : Fin dk), precision (n + 1) j = precision n j + w j) →
            (∀ (n : ℕ) (i : Fin dv) (j : Fin dk), natural (n + 1) i j = natural n i j + w j * target i j) →
              ∀ (n : ℕ) (i : Fin dv),
                CGB.Generation.associationRead (fun o j => natural n o j / precision n j) query i -
                    CGB.Generation.associationRead target query i =
                  ∑ j, query j * (p₀ j / (p₀ j + ↑n * w j)) * (m₀ i j - target i j)
doc: The one-slot retention law composes into the actual value-by-key associative readout. Each slot may have its own precision and evidence weight. The resulting terms can cancel, so the equality does not claim that an individual association survives merely because a query error is small.

name: CGB.SelfProduction.repeated_assimilation_probe_family
signature:
∀ {dv dk m : ℕ} (precision : ℕ → Fin dk → ℝ) (natural : ℕ → Fin dv → Fin dk → ℝ) (p₀ w : Fin dk → ℝ)
  (m₀ target : Fin dv → Fin dk → ℝ) (keys : Fin m → Fin dk → ℝ) (answers : Fin m → Fin dv → ℝ) (ε₀ ε : ℝ) (n : ℕ),
  (∀ (j : Fin dk), 0 < p₀ j) →
    (∀ (j : Fin dk), 0 ≤ w j) →
      (∀ (j : Fin dk), precision 0 j = p₀ j) →
        (∀ (i : Fin dv) (j : Fin dk), natural 0 i j = p₀ j * m₀ i j) →
          (∀ (t : ℕ) (j : Fin dk), precision (t + 1) j = precision t j + w j) →
            (∀ (t : ℕ) (i : Fin dv) (j : Fin dk), natural (t + 1) i j = natural t i j + w j * target i j) →
              0 ≤ ε →
                CGB.Generation.probeFamilyAccurate target keys answers ε₀ →
                  (∀ (r : Fin m) (i : Fin dv),
                      ∑ j, |keys r j * (p₀ j / (p₀ j + ↑n * w j)) * (m₀ i j - target i j)| + ε₀ ≤ ε) →
                    CGB.Generation.probeFamilyAccurate (fun i j => natural n i j / precision n j) keys answers ε
doc: A family of future queries remains accurate when its target readout is accurate and the summed retained slot deviations fit the remaining tolerance. This gives an explicit no-cancellation sufficient certificate for mixed slots.

name: CGB.SelfProduction.repeated_assimilation_retention
signature:
∀ (precision natural : ℕ → ℝ) (p₀ m₀ w target : ℝ),
  0 < p₀ →
    0 ≤ w →
      precision 0 = p₀ →
        natural 0 = p₀ * m₀ →
          (∀ (n : ℕ), precision (n + 1) = precision n + w) →
            (∀ (n : ℕ), natural (n + 1) = natural n + w * target) →
              ∀ (n : ℕ),
                precision n = p₀ + ↑n * w ∧
                  natural n / precision n - target = p₀ / (p₀ + ↑n * w) * (m₀ - target) ∧
                    (↑n * w ≤ p₀ → 1 / 2 ≤ p₀ / (p₀ + ↑n * w))
doc: With no intervening prior step, repeated identical slot evidence is accumulated by the existing natural/precision update. Its resulting mean retains exactly `p₀ / (p₀ + n*w)` of the initial error. This describes one slot in exact arithmetic, not a learned language-quality guarantee.

name: CGB.SelfProduction.sensory_loss_and_historical_interrupt_differ
signature:
∀ (δ : ℝ) (T : ℕ),
  (∀ (n : ℕ),
      CGB.Exchange.survival CGB.SensoryMaintenance.body CGB.SensoryMaintenance.world CGB.SensoryMaintenance.ec
          CGB.SensoryMaintenance.material false (fun x => CGB.SensoryMaintenance.world.sense) n =
        1) ∧
    (∀ (n : ℕ),
        7 ≤ n →
          CGB.Exchange.survival CGB.SensoryMaintenance.body CGB.SensoryMaintenance.world CGB.SensoryMaintenance.ec
              CGB.SensoryMaintenance.material true (fun x => CGB.SensoryMaintenance.world.sense) n ≤
            3 / 4) ∧
      CGB.SensoryMaintenanceRecovery.ToleratesSensoryLoss 0 1 ∧
        (∀ (n₀ duration n : ℕ),
            3 ≤ duration →
              n₀ + 3 ≤ n →
                CGB.Exchange.survival CGB.SensoryMaintenance.body CGB.SensoryMaintenance.world CGB.SensoryMaintenance.ec
                    CGB.SensoryMaintenance.material false (CGB.SensoryMaintenance.sensoryProtocol n₀ duration) n =
                  0) ∧
          (∀ (n₀ : ℕ) (w : CGB.SensoryMaintenance.world.W),
              CGB.SensoryMaintenance.body.interrupt CGB.SensoryMaintenance.world n₀ 1 n₀ w () ≠
                CGB.SensoryMaintenance.sensoryProtocol n₀ 1 n₀ w ()) ∧
            ¬CGB.SensoryMaintenance.body.Persists CGB.SensoryMaintenance.world δ T
doc: The existing sensory-maintenance witness tolerates one missing-sense tick and loses its body after three, but the historical interrupt selects its different frozen equilibrium stimulus. Thus those results cannot be silently substituted into the old `Persists` contract. The separate material reserve is a property of this witness, not a requirement on information life.

name: CGB.SelfProduction.softmax_nll_logit_error_bound
signature:
∀ {B : Type u_1} [inst : Fintype B] [Nonempty B] (z z' : B → ℝ) (target : B) (δ : ℝ),
  (∀ (b : B), |z' b - z b| ≤ δ) →
    |-Real.log (CGB.Medium.softmax z' target) - -Real.log (CGB.Medium.softmax z target)| ≤ 2 * δ
doc: If every byte logit changes by at most δ, the observed-byte negative log likelihood changes by at most 2δ. This is a per-readout bound, not a claim that the approximate state follows the reference on later ticks.

name: CGB.SelfProduction.state_conditioned_logloss_decomposition
signature:
∀ {State : Type u_1} {Byte : Type u_2} [inst : Fintype State] [inst_1 : Fintype Byte] (weight : State → ℝ)
  (law predictor : State → Byte → ℝ),
  (∀ (s : State), 0 ≤ weight s) →
    (∀ (s : State) (b : Byte), 0 ≤ law s b) →
      (∀ (s : State), ∑ b, law s b = 1) →
        (∀ (s : State) (b : Byte), 0 < predictor s b) →
          (∀ (s : State), ∑ b, predictor s b = 1) →
            ∑ s, weight s * CGB.PredictiveHarvest.crossEntropy (law s) (predictor s) =
                ∑ s, weight s * CGB.PredictiveHarvest.entropy (law s) +
                  ∑ s, weight s * CGB.InformationEnergy.kl (law s) (predictor s) ∧
              0 ≤ ∑ s, weight s * CGB.InformationEnergy.kl (law s) (predictor s)
doc: For a state-dependent predictor, expected log loss is the conditional entropy plus the state-weighted KL mismatch. This uses a specified joint law, not a new resource account, and does not assert the predictor is learned.

name: CGB.SelfProduction.state_conditioned_logloss_le_fixed
signature:
∀ {State : Type u_1} {Byte : Type u_2} [inst : Fintype State] [inst_1 : Fintype Byte] (weight : State → ℝ)
  (law : State → Byte → ℝ) (fixed : Byte → ℝ),
  (∀ (s : State), 0 ≤ weight s) →
    (∀ (s : State) (b : Byte), 0 ≤ law s b) →
      (∀ (s : State), ∑ b, law s b = 1) →
        (∀ (b : Byte), 0 < fixed b) →
          ∑ b, fixed b = 1 →
            ∑ s, weight s * CGB.PredictiveHarvest.entropy (law s) ≤
              ∑ s, weight s * CGB.PredictiveHarvest.crossEntropy (law s) fixed
doc: In a declared joint distribution, an oracle using the actual conditional byte law at each body state has no higher expected log loss than any fixed strictly positive normalized predictor. The weights are state probabilities; no additional resource state is introduced. This does not establish that the body can learn the conditional law, or that prediction improves viability.

name: CGB.SelfProduction.stationary_nonincreasing_loss_flat_on_existing_cycle
signature:
∀ (loss : CGB.RenewableLearning.Cell → ℝ),
  (∀ (n : ℕ),
      loss
          (CGB.SelfProduction.trajectory
            (CGB.SelfProduction.renewableLanguageContract CGB.SelfProduction.existingRenewableCarrier) (n + 1)) ≤
        loss
          (CGB.SelfProduction.trajectory
            (CGB.SelfProduction.renewableLanguageContract CGB.SelfProduction.existingRenewableCarrier) n)) →
    loss CGB.RenewableLearning.Cell.aSpent = loss CGB.RenewableLearning.Cell.search ∧
      loss CGB.RenewableLearning.Cell.aReady = loss CGB.RenewableLearning.Cell.aSpent ∧
        loss CGB.RenewableLearning.Cell.search = loss CGB.RenewableLearning.Cell.aReady
doc: On the existing closed three-state witness, a fixed state-dependent loss that never increases cannot strictly improve anywhere in the cycle. In particular, recurrent strict improvement against one stationary law requires allowing loss increases, changing the state/world, or changing the comparison. This does not constrain a nonperiodic open-world trajectory.

name: CGB.SelfProduction.stochastic_joint_recovery_policy_generation
signature:
∀ {State : Type u_1} {World : Type u_2} {Act : Type u_3} {Event : Type u_4} [inst : Fintype State]
  [inst_1 : DecidableEq State] [inst_2 : Fintype World] [inst_3 : DecidableEq World] [inst_4 : Fintype Event]
  (P : CGB.Interaction.Machine (State × World) Act Event) (viable : State × World → Prop) (seed : State × World),
  viable seed →
    ∀ (rank : State × World → ℕ) (horizon : ℕ) (mark : ℕ → State × World → Event → State × World → Bool),
      (∀ (z : State × World), viable z → rank z < horizon) →
        (∀ (s : State),
            ∃ a,
              ∀ (t : ℕ) (w : World) (e : Event) (z' : State × World),
                viable (s, w) →
                  0 < P.step a (s, w) e z' → viable z' ∧ (mark t (s, w) e z' = false → rank z' < rank (s, w))) →
          ∃ policy process,
            (∀ (t : ℕ) (z : State × World) (e : Event) (z' : State × World),
                process.step t z e z' = P.step (policy z.1) z e z') ∧
              (∀ (n : ℕ) (z : State × World), ¬viable z → CGB.Energetics.law process seed n z = 0) ∧
                ∀ (t : ℕ) (z : State × World),
                  viable z → CGB.EventChannels.Kernel.firstHit (CGB.Energetics.events process) mark t horizon z = 1
doc: Generate one stochastic policy whose same closed loop both stays within the joint region and reaches the declared event within the finite horizon. The decreasing rank is a proof certificate, not stored body state. The mark must be connected separately to an actual useful event in the world.

name: CGB.SelfProduction.stochastic_joint_viability_policy_generation
signature:
∀ {State : Type u_1} {World : Type u_2} {Act : Type u_3} {Event : Type u_4} [inst : Fintype State]
  [inst_1 : DecidableEq State] [inst_2 : Fintype World] [inst_3 : DecidableEq World] [inst_4 : Fintype Event]
  (P : CGB.Interaction.Machine (State × World) Act Event) (viable : State × World → Prop) (seed : State × World),
  viable seed →
    ((∀ (s : State),
        ∃ a, ∀ (w : World) (e : Event) (z' : State × World), viable (s, w) → 0 < P.step a (s, w) e z' → viable z') ↔
      ∃ policy,
        (∀ (s : State) (w : World) (e : Event) (z' : State × World),
            viable (s, w) → 0 < P.step (policy s) (s, w) e z' → viable z') ∧
          ∃ process,
            (∀ (t : ℕ) (z : State × World) (e : Event) (z' : State × World),
                process.step t z e z' = P.step (policy z.1) z e z') ∧
              ∀ (n : ℕ) (z : State × World), ¬viable z → CGB.Energetics.law process seed n z = 0)
doc: Stochastic version: a body-only policy keeps every positive-probability successor in the joint viable region iff each body has an action safe for all compatible viable worlds and all supported events. The generated closed-loop law has zero mass outside the region at every finite tick. This is not an infinite-path measure or a proof that the safe-action premise is populated by a real language world.

name: CGB.SelfProduction.trajectory_viable
signature:
∀ {S : Type u_1} {A : Type u_2} {I : Type u_3} (c : CGB.SelfProduction.Contract S A I) (n : ℕ),
  c.viable (CGB.SelfProduction.trajectory c n)
doc: The same rule generates a valid state at every finite time.

name: CGB.SelfProduction.two_phase_finite_score_step_improves
signature:
∀ {B : Type u_1} [inst : Fintype B] [inst_1 : DecidableEq B] (z : B → ℝ) (target : B) (η : ℝ),
  0 < η →
    (∃ b, b ≠ target) →
      CGB.Medium.softmax z target <
        CGB.Medium.softmax (fun b => z b + η * ((if b = target then 1 else 0) - CGB.Medium.softmax z b)) target
doc: On a finite alphabet with at least two symbols, a positive finite two-phase score step strictly improves the probability of the observed symbol on the same frozen feature. It does not assert future improvement.

name: CGB.SelfProduction.uniform_block_learning_failure_decay
doc: Minimal probabilistic upgrade for persistent learning: if the probability of no useful learning event after `n` completed blocks is `q n`, and every block has conditional success at least `p`, then failure is bounded by `(1-p)^n`. This is an abstract finite-prefix inequality; a real infinite process must separately prove the conditional minorization premise.

name: CGB.SurvivalBounds.cumulative_risk_lower
signature: ∀ (q risk : ℕ → ℝ), (∀ (n : ℕ), q n - risk n ≤ q (n + 1)) → ∀ (n : ℕ), q 0 - ∑ k ∈ Finset.range n, risk k ≤ q n
doc: Telescoping lower bound; no independence, absorption, or sign premise is needed for this algebraic statement. Nonnegative `risk` gives its risk reading.

name: CGB.SurvivalBounds.decay_eventually_lt
doc: Reuse the existing geometric bound; no nonnegativity of `q` is needed for this upper-tail conclusion. For survival, each index can denote a completed block.

name: CGB.SurvivalBounds.expectedLifetime_strict_of_row_gap
signature:
∀ {S : Type u_1} {O : Type u_2} [inst : Fintype S] [inst_1 : DecidableEq S] [inst_2 : Fintype O]
  (normal cut : CGB.Interaction.Machine S ℕ O) (initial : S) (a : S → ℝ),
  (∀ (s : S), 0 ≤ a s ∧ a s ≤ 1) →
    a initial = 1 →
      ∀ (pN pC : ℝ),
        0 ≤ pN →
          pN < pC →
            pC ≤ 1 →
              (∀ (t : ℕ) (s : S), (1 - pN) * a s ≤ ∑ o, ∑ s', normal.step t s o s' * a s') →
                (∀ (t : ℕ) (s : S), ∑ o, ∑ s', cut.step t s o s' * a s' ≤ (1 - pC) * a s) →
                  ∀ (T : ℕ),
                    2 ≤ T →
                      CGB.SurvivalBounds.expectedLifetime cut initial a T <
                        CGB.SurvivalBounds.expectedLifetime normal initial a T
doc: Positive maintenance without immortality: the same initial individual and observable have strictly longer truncated lifetime under the normal process. The advantage is strict at tick 1 and nonnegative at every tick.

name: CGB.SurvivalBounds.expected_step
signature:
∀ {S : Type u_1} {O : Type u_2} [inst : Fintype S] [inst_1 : DecidableEq S] [inst_2 : Fintype O]
  (P : CGB.Interaction.Machine S ℕ O) (initial : S) (v : S → ℝ) (t : ℕ),
  CGB.Energetics.mean (CGB.Energetics.law P initial (t + 1)) v =
    ∑ s, CGB.Energetics.law P initial t s * ∑ o, ∑ s', P.step t s o s' * v s'
doc: General expected-step identity extracted from the rearrangement in `Energetics.expected_first_law`. The observable is not an energy `Account`.

name: CGB.SurvivalBounds.finite_window_lifetime_transfer
signature:
∀ (qN qC rN rC : ℕ → ℝ) (T : ℕ) (E_N E_C tailBound : ℝ),
  (∀ (n : ℕ), 0 ≤ rN n) →
    (∀ (L : ℕ), ∑ k ∈ Finset.range L, rC (T + k) ≤ tailBound) →
      |∑ t ∈ Finset.range T, rN t - ∑ t ∈ Finset.range T, qN t| ≤ E_N →
        |∑ t ∈ Finset.range T, rC t - ∑ t ∈ Finset.range T, qC t| ≤ E_C →
          E_N + E_C + tailBound < ∑ t ∈ Finset.range T, qN t - ∑ t ∈ Finset.range T, qC t →
            ∀ (N : ℕ), T ≤ N → ∑ t ∈ Finset.range N, rC t < ∑ t ∈ Finset.range N, rN t
doc: Finite-window cumulative errors plus an actual cut-tail certificate transfer reference lifetime advantage to every actual horizon beyond the window.

name: CGB.SurvivalBounds.geometric_lower
doc: Lower counterpart to the reused geometric upper bound.

name: CGB.SurvivalBounds.geometric_tail_bound
doc: Uniform scalar decay bounds every finite cut tail, reusing the existing pointwise geometric bound rather than repeating its power induction.

name: CGB.SurvivalBounds.mean_contraction
signature:
∀ {S : Type u_1} {O : Type u_2} [inst : Fintype S] [inst_1 : DecidableEq S] [inst_2 : Fintype O]
  (P : CGB.Interaction.Machine S ℕ O) (initial : S) (v : S → ℝ) (p : ℝ) (t : ℕ),
  (∀ (s : S), ∑ o, ∑ s', P.step t s o s' * v s' ≤ (1 - p) * v s) →
    CGB.Energetics.mean (CGB.Energetics.law P initial (t + 1)) v ≤
      (1 - p) * CGB.Energetics.mean (CGB.Energetics.law P initial t) v
doc: A local row contraction transfers to the original ensemble score.

name: CGB.SurvivalBounds.mean_initial
signature:
∀ {S : Type u_1} {O : Type u_2} [inst : Fintype S] [inst_1 : DecidableEq S] [inst_2 : Fintype O]
  (P : CGB.Interaction.Machine S ℕ O) (initial : S) (v : S → ℝ),
  CGB.Energetics.mean (CGB.Energetics.law P initial 0) v = v initial

name: CGB.SurvivalBounds.mean_retention_step
signature:
∀ {S : Type u_1} {O : Type u_2} [inst : Fintype S] [inst_1 : DecidableEq S] [inst_2 : Fintype O]
  (P : CGB.Interaction.Machine S ℕ O) (initial : S) (v : S → ℝ) (p : ℝ) (t : ℕ),
  (∀ (s : S), (1 - p) * v s ≤ ∑ o, ∑ s', P.step t s o s' * v s') →
    (1 - p) * CGB.Energetics.mean (CGB.Energetics.law P initial t) v ≤
      CGB.Energetics.mean (CGB.Energetics.law P initial (t + 1)) v
doc: Lower multiplicative row bounds transfer along the same actual law.

name: CGB.SurvivalBounds.mean_risk_step
signature:
∀ {S : Type u_1} {O : Type u_2} [inst : Fintype S] [inst_1 : DecidableEq S] [inst_2 : Fintype O]
  (P : CGB.Interaction.Machine S ℕ O) (initial : S) (v : S → ℝ) (risk : ℝ) (t : ℕ),
  (∀ (s : S), v s - risk ≤ ∑ o, ∑ s', P.step t s o s' * v s') →
    CGB.Energetics.mean (CGB.Energetics.law P initial t) v - risk ≤
      CGB.Energetics.mean (CGB.Energetics.law P initial (t + 1)) v
doc: A local additive risk allowance transfers without independence assumptions.

name: CGB.SurvivalBounds.mean_unit_interval
signature:
∀ {S : Type u_1} {O : Type u_2} [inst : Fintype S] [inst_1 : DecidableEq S] [inst_2 : Fintype O]
  (P : CGB.Interaction.Machine S ℕ O) (initial : S) (v : S → ℝ),
  (∀ (s : S), 0 ≤ v s ∧ v s ≤ 1) →
    ∀ (t : ℕ),
      0 ≤ CGB.Energetics.mean (CGB.Energetics.law P initial t) v ∧
        CGB.Energetics.mean (CGB.Energetics.law P initial t) v ≤ 1
doc: A bounded observable gives a bounded score under the actual process law.

name: CGB.SurvivalBounds.no_uniform_positive_lower
doc: Uniform positive irreversible block loss rules out a fixed positive floor.

name: CGB.SurvivalBounds.normal_cut_eventual_gap
signature:
∀ {S : Type u_1} {O : Type u_2} [inst : Fintype S] [inst_1 : DecidableEq S] [inst_2 : Fintype O]
  (normal cut : CGB.Interaction.Machine S ℕ O) (initial : S) (v : S → ℝ),
  (∀ (s : S), 0 ≤ v s ∧ v s ≤ 1) →
    v initial = 1 →
      ∀ (risk : ℕ → ℝ) (δ p : ℝ),
        δ < 1 →
          0 < p →
            p ≤ 1 →
              (∀ (n : ℕ), ∑ k ∈ Finset.range n, risk k ≤ δ) →
                (∀ (t : ℕ) (s : S), v s - risk t ≤ ∑ o, ∑ s', normal.step t s o s' * v s') →
                  (∀ (t : ℕ) (s : S), ∑ o, ∑ s', cut.step t s o s' * v s' ≤ (1 - p) * v s) →
                    (∀ (n : ℕ), 1 - δ ≤ CGB.Energetics.mean (CGB.Energetics.law normal initial n) v) ∧
                      ∃ N,
                        ∀ (n : ℕ),
                          N ≤ n →
                            (1 - δ) / 2 <
                              CGB.Energetics.mean (CGB.Energetics.law normal initial n) v -
                                CGB.Energetics.mean (CGB.Energetics.law cut initial n) v
doc: Stronger, separate all-time-floor criterion: SAME initial state and observable, normal prefix risk budget versus uniform cut contraction. The row premises must be verified on those two processes. No infinite-path measure is assumed.

name: CGB.SurvivalBounds.prefix_gap_persists
signature:
∀ (normal cut : ℕ → ℝ) (T : ℕ) (tailBound : ℝ),
  (∀ (n : ℕ), 0 ≤ normal n) →
    (∀ (L : ℕ), ∑ k ∈ Finset.range L, cut (T + k) ≤ tailBound) →
      tailBound < ∑ t ∈ Finset.range T, normal t - ∑ t ∈ Finset.range T, cut t →
        ∀ (N : ℕ), T ≤ N → ∑ t ∈ Finset.range N, cut t < ∑ t ∈ Finset.range N, normal t
doc: A prefix advantage exceeding the entire cut-tail allowance persists at all later horizons; normal needs only nonnegative scores, not contraction.

name: CGB.SurvivalBounds.risk_budget_uniform_lower
signature:
∀ (q risk : ℕ → ℝ) (δ : ℝ),
  q 0 = 1 →
    (∀ (n : ℕ), q n - risk n ≤ q (n + 1)) → (∀ (n : ℕ), ∑ k ∈ Finset.range n, risk k ≤ δ) → ∀ (n : ℕ), 1 - δ ≤ q n
doc: A prefix budget allows strictly positive but summably bounded per-step risk. It does not require `δ < 1`; that premise is needed only for a positive floor.

name: CGB.Unified.balanced_allocation_contract
signature:
∀ {p : ℝ},

name: CGB.Unified.balanced_allocation_interaction

name: CGB.Unified.balanced_nonneg

name: CGB.Unified.balanced_row_budget

name: CGB.Unified.bernoulli_expected_brier_calibrated
signature: ∀ (p q : ℝ), CGB.Unified.bernoulliExpectedBrier p q ≤ CGB.Unified.bernoulliExpectedBrier q q

name: CGB.Unified.bernoulli_expected_brier_gap

name: CGB.Unified.bernoulli_prediction_error_expectation

signature: CGB.Unified.bernoulliBrierScore (1 / 2) 0 ≠ CGB.Unified.bernoulliPredictionError (1 / 2) 0

name: CGB.Unified.build_has_competition_and_differentiation
signature:
∀ (κ base kp km p₀ γ R ρ : ℝ) (carrier : CGB.LanguageLifeKernel.ConservedCarrierPath) {p : ℝ},
  0 ≤ p →
    p ≤ 1 →
      CGB.Continual.Nonneg ((CGB.Unified.build κ base kp km p₀ γ R ρ carrier).allocation p) ∧
        CGB.Continual.ColBudget ((CGB.Unified.build κ base kp km p₀ γ R ρ carrier).allocation p) ∧
          CGB.Continual.RowBudget ((CGB.Unified.build κ base kp km p₀ γ R ρ carrier).allocation p)

name: CGB.Unified.build_history_balance
signature:
∀ (κ base kp km p₀ γ R ρ : ℝ) (carrier : CGB.LanguageLifeKernel.ConservedCarrierPath) (k : ℕ),
  (CGB.Unified.build κ base kp km p₀ γ R ρ carrier).carrier.value k -
      (CGB.Unified.build κ base kp km p₀ γ R ρ carrier).carrier.value 0 =
    ∑ n ∈ Finset.range k,
      ((CGB.Unified.build κ base kp km p₀ γ R ρ carrier).carrier.input n -
        (CGB.Unified.build κ base kp km p₀ γ R ρ carrier).carrier.output n)
doc: The supplied typed carrier exposes its telescoping conserved history.

name: CGB.Unified.build_history_is_geometric
signature:
∀ (κ base kp km p₀ γ R ρ : ℝ) (carrier : CGB.LanguageLifeKernel.ConservedCarrierPath),
  kp + km ≠ 0 →
    ∀ (t : ℕ),
      (CGB.Unified.build κ base kp km p₀ γ R ρ carrier).history t - kp / (kp + km) =
        (1 - kp - km) ^ t * (p₀ - kp / (kp + km))
doc: The retained history is the geometric trace generated by two-state exchange.

name: CGB.Unified.build_is_cgb_candidate

name: CGB.Unified.build_latch_holds_and_releases

name: CGB.Unified.build_mechanical_admission
signature:
∀ (κ base kp km p₀ γ R ρ : ℝ) (carrier : CGB.LanguageLifeKernel.ConservedCarrierPath),
  κ ≠ 0 →
    0 < base →
      ∀ {p : ℝ},
        0 ≤ p →
          p ≤ 1 →
            1 < γ →
              0 < R →
                R / γ ≤ ρ →
                  ρ ≤ R * γ →
                    kp + km ≠ 0 →
                      ∀ (t : ℕ),
                        CGB.Generation.CGBOptimizerCandidate (CGB.Unified.build κ base kp km p₀ γ R ρ carrier).relation
                            (CGB.Unified.build κ base kp km p₀ γ R ρ carrier).gain ∧
                          CGB.Continual.Nonneg ((CGB.Unified.build κ base kp km p₀ γ R ρ carrier).allocation p) ∧
                            CGB.Continual.ColBudget ((CGB.Unified.build κ base kp km p₀ γ R ρ carrier).allocation p) ∧
                              CGB.Continual.RowBudget ((CGB.Unified.build κ base kp km p₀ γ R ρ carrier).allocation p) ∧
                                (CGB.Unified.build κ base kp km p₀ γ R ρ carrier).history t - kp / (kp + km) =
                                    (1 - kp - km) ^ t * (p₀ - kp / (kp + km)) ∧
                                  R / γ ≤ (CGB.Unified.build κ base kp km p₀ γ R ρ carrier).modulation false ∧
                                    (CGB.Unified.build κ base kp km p₀ γ R ρ carrier).modulation false ≤ R * γ

name: _private.CGBAxioms.GenerationInformationProjection.0.CGB.InformationProjection.marginals_pos
signature:
∀ {β : Type u_1} {γ : Type u_2} [inst : Fintype β] [inst_1 : Fintype γ] (p : β → γ → ℝ),
  (∀ (b : β) (c : γ), 0 ≤ p b c) →
    ∀ (b : β) (c : γ), 0 < p b c → 0 < ∑ c', p b c' ∧ 0 < ∑ b', p b' c ∧ 0 < ∑ b', ∑ c', p b' c'

name: _private.CGBAxioms.GenerationInformationProjection.0.CGB.InformationProjection.project_sum
signature:
∀ {β : Type u_1} {γ : Type u_2} {δ : Type u_3} [inst : Fintype β] [inst_1 : Fintype γ] (f : γ → δ) (p : β → γ → ℝ)

name: _private.CGBAxioms.GenerationSelfProduction.0.CGB.SelfProduction.closed_region_law_zero
signature:
∀ {S : Type u_1} {E : Type u_2} [inst : Fintype S] [inst_1 : DecidableEq S] [inst_2 : Fintype E]
  (Q : CGB.Interaction.Machine S ℕ E) (region : S → Prop) (seed : S),
  region seed →
    (∀ (t : ℕ) (x : S) (e : E) (y : S), region x → 0 < Q.step t x e y → region y) →
      ∀ (n : ℕ) (z : S), ¬region z → CGB.Energetics.law Q seed n z = 0

name: CGB.GDNLife.Process.externalInformation_nonneg
signature:
∀ (joint : CGB.GDNLife.Byte → CGB.GDNLife.Byte → ℝ),
  (∀ (now later : CGB.GDNLife.Byte), 0 ≤ joint now later) → 0 ≤ CGB.GDNLife.Process.externalInformation joint
doc: A valid external language law has nonnegative information opportunity. This is finite conditional mutual information, rather than an arbitrary natural-number intake signal.

name: CGB.GDNLife.Process.externallyUseful_improves
signature:
∀ {k d : ℕ} {Act : Type u_1} {World : Type u_2} (P : CGB.GDNLife.Process k d Act World) (n : ℕ),
  P.externallyUseful n →
    CGB.GDNLife.nll (P.scores (n + 1)) (P.arrival (n + 1)).byte < CGB.GDNLife.nll (P.scores n) (P.arrival (n + 1)).byte
doc: The useful-event certificate invokes the earlier causal result; it does not inspect the next byte while preparing the current prediction.

name: CGB.GDNLife.Process.future_reserve_preserved_keeps_signature_distinction
signature:
∀ {k d : ℕ} (M : CGB.GDNLife.Model k d) {m n : ℕ} (Q : CGB.GDNLife.Process.ExternalFutureProbes m)
  (before after : Fin n → CGB.GDNLife.State k d) (i j : Fin n),
  CGB.GDNLife.Process.futureReservePreserved M Q before after →
    CGB.GDNLife.Process.futureLanguageSignature M Q (before i) ≠
        CGB.GDNLife.Process.futureLanguageSignature M Q (before j) →
      CGB.GDNLife.Process.futureLanguageSignature M Q (after i) ≠
        CGB.GDNLife.Process.futureLanguageSignature M Q (after j)
doc: A preserved future-language reserve cannot silently merge two histories that a registered external continuation could previously distinguish. This is the long-delay retention condition for any causal difference already carried by the body; it adds neither an action log nor a separate eligibility state.

name: CGB.GDNLife.Process.future_reserve_recoverable_iff
signature:
∀ {k d : ℕ} (M : CGB.GDNLife.Model k d) {m n : ℕ} (Q : CGB.GDNLife.Process.ExternalFutureProbes m)
  (before after : Fin n → CGB.GDNLife.State k d),
  (∃ restore,
      ∀ (i : Fin n),
        restore (CGB.GDNLife.Process.futureLanguageSignature M Q (after i)) =
          CGB.GDNLife.Process.futureLanguageSignature M Q (before i)) ↔
    CGB.GDNLife.Process.futureReservePreserved M Q before after
doc: A future distinction is not dissipated exactly when all of the prior future language signature remains readable from the post-update signature. This reuses the existing causal-carrier theorem instead of introducing a separate retention mechanism.

name: CGB.GDNLife.Process.loses_future_language_distinction_iff_not_preserved
signature:
∀ {k d : ℕ} (M : CGB.GDNLife.Model k d) {m n : ℕ} (Q : CGB.GDNLife.Process.ExternalFutureProbes m)
  (before after : Fin n → CGB.GDNLife.State k d),
  CGB.GDNLife.Process.losesFutureLanguageDistinction M Q before after ↔
    ¬CGB.GDNLife.Process.futureReservePreserved M Q before after
doc: Merging a prior distinct future-language signature is precisely the failure of that causal retention contract.

name: CGB.GDNLife.Process.next_byte_improves
signature:
∀ {k d : ℕ} {Act : Type u_1} {World : Type u_2} (P : CGB.GDNLife.Process k d Act World) (n : ℕ) (δ : ℝ),
  (P.arrival (n + 1)).byte = (P.arrival n).byte →
    (∀ (b : CGB.GDNLife.Byte),
        |P.scores (n + 1) b -
              CGB.GDNLife.logits (CGB.GDNLife.finish P.model (P.snapshot n) (P.arrival n)) (P.snapshot n).feature b| ≤
          δ) →
      2 * δ <
          CGB.GDNLife.nll (P.scores n) (P.arrival n).byte -
            CGB.GDNLife.nll
              (CGB.GDNLife.logits (CGB.GDNLife.finish P.model (P.snapshot n) (P.arrival n)) (P.snapshot n).feature)
              (P.arrival n).byte →
        CGB.GDNLife.nll (P.scores (n + 1)) (P.arrival (n + 1)).byte <
          CGB.GDNLife.nll (P.scores n) (P.arrival (n + 1)).byte
doc: Repetition refers to the world's actual next byte, not a byte chosen for rescoring. The readout-drift budget includes the next physical-time prior.

name: CGB.GDNLife.Process.recurrent_external_evidence_forces_activity
signature:
∀ {k d : ℕ} {Act : Type u_1} {World : Type u_2} (P : CGB.GDNLife.Process k d Act World) (passive : Act),
  (CGB.ActiveInference.eventuallyPassive (fun n => P.policy (P.run n).1) passive →
      ∃ N, ∀ (n : ℕ), N ≤ n → ¬P.externallyUseful n) →
    (∀ (N : ℕ), ∃ n, N ≤ n ∧ P.externallyUseful n) →
      ¬CGB.ActiveInference.eventuallyPassive (fun n => P.policy (P.run n).1) passive
doc: If settling into a passive policy rules out recurrent externally useful language, but such events actually recur on this same trajectory, the policy cannot settle. This is the language form of active necessity: no arbitrary `intake`, opportunity counter, food pool, or maintenance currency is added.

name: CGB.GDNLife.Process.recurrent_external_information_forces_activity
signature:
∀ {k d : ℕ} {Act : Type u_1} {World : Type u_2} (P : CGB.GDNLife.Process k d Act World) (L : P.ExternalLanguageLaw)
  (passive : Act),
  (CGB.ActiveInference.eventuallyPassive (fun n => P.policy (P.run n).1) passive →
      ∃ N, ∀ (n : ℕ), N ≤ n → L.information (P.run n).1 (P.policy (P.run n).1) = 0) →
    (∀ (N : ℕ),
        ∃ n,
          N ≤ n ∧
            (P.arrival n).source = CGB.GDNLife.Source.external ∧ 0 < L.information (P.run n).1 (P.policy (P.run n).1)) →
      ¬CGB.ActiveInference.eventuallyPassive (fun n => P.policy (P.run n).1) passive
doc: Information-theoretic active necessity for the concrete GDN port. If settling into `passive` eliminates the conditional information available from the external language boundary, while positive external information recurs on the realised trajectory, the policy cannot settle into `passive`. The premise is deliberately a boundary statement, not a synthetic hunger counter. To turn available information into a learning claim, it must also meet the causal `externallyUseful` scoring certificate above.

name: CGB.GDNLife.Process.run_body_step
signature:
∀ {k d : ℕ} {Act : Type u_1} {World : Type u_2} (P : CGB.GDNLife.Process k d Act World) (n : ℕ),
  (P.run (n + 1)).1 = CGB.GDNLife.finish P.model (P.snapshot n) (P.arrival n)

name: CGB.GDNLife.Process.run_initial
signature:
∀ {k d : ℕ} {Act : Type u_1} {World : Type u_2} (P : CGB.GDNLife.Process k d Act World),
  P.run 0 = (P.initial, P.worldInitial)

name: CGB.GDNLife.Process.run_positive
signature:
∀ {k d : ℕ} {Act : Type u_1} {World : Type u_2} (P : CGB.GDNLife.Process k d Act World) (n : ℕ),
  CGB.GDNLife.Positive (P.run n).1

name: CGB.GDNLife.Process.run_step
signature:
∀ {k d : ℕ} {Act : Type u_1} {World : Type u_2} (P : CGB.GDNLife.Process k d Act World) (n : ℕ),
  P.run (n + 1) =
    (CGB.GDNLife.step P.model (P.run n).1 (P.arrival n),
      P.evolve (P.run n).2 (P.run n).1 (P.policy (P.run n).1) (P.arrival n))

name: CGB.GDNLife.Process.scored_external_language_trajectory
signature:
∀ {k d : ℕ} {Act : Type u_1} {World : Type u_2} (P : CGB.GDNLife.Process k d Act World),
  0 < P.model.headStep →
    ∀ (passive : Act),
      (CGB.ActiveInference.eventuallyPassive (fun n => P.policy (P.run n).1) passive →
          ∃ N, ∀ (n : ℕ), N ≤ n → ¬P.externallyUseful n) →
        (∀ (N : ℕ), ∃ n, N ≤ n ∧ P.externallyUseful n) →
          (∃ n a a', (P.boundary (P.run n).2 (P.run n).1 a).byte ≠ (P.boundary (P.run n).2 (P.run n).1 a').byte) →
            (∀ (n : ℕ), CGB.GDNLife.nll (P.scores n) (P.arrival n).byte < Real.log 256) →
              (∀ (n : ℕ), CGB.GDNLife.Positive (P.run n).1) ∧
                ¬CGB.ActiveInference.eventuallyPassive (fun n => P.policy (P.run n).1) passive ∧
                  (¬∃ predict,
                        ∀ (n : ℕ) (a : Act),
                          predict (P.run n).2 (P.run n).1 = (P.boundary (P.run n).2 (P.run n).1 a).byte) ∧
                    (∀ (n : ℕ), 0 < Real.log 256 - CGB.GDNLife.nll (P.scores n) (P.arrival n).byte) ∧
                      (∀ (N : ℕ),
                          ∃ n,
                            N ≤ n ∧
                              CGB.GDNLife.nll (P.scores (n + 1)) (P.arrival (n + 1)).byte <
                                CGB.GDNLife.nll (P.scores n) (P.arrival (n + 1)).byte) ∧
                        ¬∃ N, ∀ (n : ℕ), N ≤ n → (P.run (n + 1)).1 = (P.run n).1
doc: Conditional language-level joint result for the real GDN. Every condition is about the actual language trajectory: source provenance, recurrent post-update improvement, the causal effect of action on the next arrival, and a non-uniform prequential margin. The result intentionally says nothing about physical food, material ingestion, or an auxiliary reserve state. It is still not a full `Medium.Lives` construction.

name: CGB.GDNLife.Process.scored_joint_trajectory
signature:
∀ {k d : ℕ} {Act : Type u_1} {World : Type u_2} (P : CGB.GDNLife.Process k d Act World),
  0 < P.model.headStep →
    ∀ (intake : World → CGB.GDNLife.State k d → Act → CGB.GDNLife.Arrival → ℕ) (passive : Act),
      CGB.ActiveInference.unbounded (P.signal intake) →
        ∀ (opportunity : CGB.GDNLife.State k d × World → ℕ),
          (∀ (z : CGB.GDNLife.State k d × World),
              opportunity (P.contract.step z (P.contract.response z passive)) +
                  intake z.2 z.1 passive (P.boundary z.2 z.1 passive) ≤
                opportunity z) →
            (∃ n a a', (P.boundary (P.run n).2 (P.run n).1 a).byte ≠ (P.boundary (P.run n).2 (P.run n).1 a').byte) →
              ∀ (m : ℝ),
                0 ≤ m →
                  (∀ (n : ℕ), CGB.GDNLife.nll (P.scores n) (P.arrival n).byte < Real.log 256 - m) →
                    (∀ (N : ℕ),
                        ∃ n,
                          N ≤ n ∧
                            ∃ δ,
                              (P.arrival (n + 1)).byte = (P.arrival n).byte ∧
                                (∀ (b : CGB.GDNLife.Byte),
                                    |P.scores (n + 1) b -
                                          CGB.GDNLife.logits (CGB.GDNLife.finish P.model (P.snapshot n) (P.arrival n))
                                            (P.snapshot n).feature b| ≤
                                      δ) ∧
                                  2 * δ <
                                    CGB.GDNLife.nll (P.scores n) (P.arrival n).byte -
                                      CGB.GDNLife.nll
                                        (CGB.GDNLife.logits (CGB.GDNLife.finish P.model (P.snapshot n) (P.arrival n))
                                          (P.snapshot n).feature)
                                        (P.arrival n).byte) →
                      (∀ (n : ℕ), CGB.GDNLife.Positive (P.run n).1) ∧
                        ¬CGB.ActiveInference.eventuallyPassive (fun n => P.policy (P.run n).1) passive ∧
                          (¬∃ predict,
                                ∀ (n : ℕ) (a : Act),
                                  predict (P.run n).2 (P.run n).1 = (P.boundary (P.run n).2 (P.run n).1 a).byte) ∧
                            (∀ (n : ℕ),
                                0 < Real.log 256 - CGB.GDNLife.nll (P.scores n) (P.arrival n).byte ∧
                                  0 < Real.log 256 - CGB.GDNLife.nll (P.scores n) (P.arrival n).byte - m) ∧
                              (∀ (N : ℕ),
                                  ∃ n,
                                    N ≤ n ∧
                                      CGB.GDNLife.nll (P.scores (n + 1)) (P.arrival (n + 1)).byte <
                                        CGB.GDNLife.nll (P.scores n) (P.arrival (n + 1)).byte) ∧
                                ¬∃ N, ∀ (n : ℕ), N ≤ n → (P.run (n + 1)).1 = (P.run n).1
doc: A conditional scored joint trajectory for this real GDN. Conditions are on the actual world: registered intake, a finite passive opportunity budget under the same intervenable transition, an action contrast, a nonnegative predictive margin, and recurrent next-byte persistence with bounded readout drift. Recurrent future score gain is *derived*, not supplied as `hlearn`. Numeric positivity is still not material/biological viability. This deterministic-world statement scores actual future bytes, not a claim about the conditional law of an unspecified stochastic language world.

name: CGB.GDNLife.Process.self_not_externallyUseful
signature:
∀ {k d : ℕ} {Act : Type u_1} {World : Type u_2} (P : CGB.GDNLife.Process k d Act World) (n : ℕ),
  (P.arrival n).source = CGB.GDNLife.Source.self → ¬P.externallyUseful n
doc: A copied self byte never becomes external evidence just by passing through the same learning rule. It can still affect the body through `step`.

name: CGB.GDNLife.Process.self_speech_action_contrast_writes_body
signature:
∀ {k d : ℕ} {Act : Type u_1} {World : Type u_2} (P : CGB.GDNLife.Process k d Act World) (n : ℕ) (a₀ a₁ : Act),
  (P.boundary (P.run n).2 (P.run n).1 a₀).source = CGB.GDNLife.Source.self →
    (P.boundary (P.run n).2 (P.run n).1 a₁).source = CGB.GDNLife.Source.self →
      0 < (P.boundary (P.run n).2 (P.run n).1 a₀).observationPrecision →
        0 < (P.boundary (P.run n).2 (P.run n).1 a₁).observationPrecision →
          (P.boundary (P.run n).2 (P.run n).1 a₀).byte ≠ (P.boundary (P.run n).2 (P.run n).1 a₁).byte →
            CGB.GDNLife.step P.model (P.run n).1 (P.boundary (P.run n).2 (P.run n).1 a₀) ≠
              CGB.GDNLife.step P.model (P.run n).1 (P.boundary (P.run n).2 (P.run n).1 a₁)
doc: Two candidate language actions that emit different live self-produced bytes write distinct next bodies through the ordinary GDN boundary transition. The byte is the action's existing bodily consequence, not a separately stored action record.

name: CGB.Generation.BodyCausalCarrier.merged_history_preserves_read_and_successor
signature:
∀ {U : Type u_1} {Λ : Type u_2} {A : Type u_3} {I : Type u_4} {History : Type u_5} {Arrival : Type u_6}
  {Readout : Type u_7} {Carrier : Type u_8} {M : CGB.Medium U Λ A I} (K : CGB.Generation.BodyCausalCarrier M),
  (∀ (h h' : History), K.state (K.encode h) = K.state (K.encode h') → K.required h = K.required h') ∧
    ∀ (h h' : History),
      K.state (K.encode h) = K.state (K.encode h') →
        ∀ (a : Arrival), K.state (K.encode (K.advance h a)) = K.state (K.encode (K.advance h' a))
doc: Equivalently, any two histories merged by the carrier agree on every declared readout and on the carrier successor for each arrival.

name: CGB.Generation.BodyCausalCarrier.satisfies_causal_carrier_contract
signature:
∀ {U : Type u_1} {Λ : Type u_2} {A : Type u_3} {I : Type u_4} {History : Type u_5} {Arrival : Type u_6}
  {Readout : Type u_7} {Carrier : Type u_8} {M : CGB.Medium U Λ A I} (K : CGB.Generation.BodyCausalCarrier M),
  ∃ read next,
    (∀ (h : History), read (K.state (K.encode h)) = K.required h) ∧
      ∀ (h : History) (a : Arrival), next (K.state (K.encode h)) a = K.state (K.encode (K.advance h a))
doc: The carrier fields meet the existing exact readout-and-successor contract. This is a use of the actual body step, not a second recurrence.

name: CGB.Generation.LocalColumnProjections.activity_unchanged_outside
doc: P1b makes a nonparticipant's activity readout unchanged under the same physical event. No independent activity update is permitted.

name: CGB.Generation.LocalColumnProjections.carrier_unchanged_outside
doc: The same event leaves a nonparticipant's local causal reading unchanged.

name: CGB.Generation.LocalColumnProjections.contact_unchanged_outside
doc: A contact reading changes only when at least one endpoint participates.

name: CGB.GDNLife.Process.ExternalLanguageLaw.information_nonneg
signature:
∀ {k d : ℕ} {Act : Type u_1} {World : Type u_2} {P : CGB.GDNLife.Process k d Act World} (L : P.ExternalLanguageLaw)
  (s : CGB.GDNLife.State k d) (a : Act), 0 ≤ L.information s a
doc: The state/action-indexed opportunity inherits CMI nonnegativity from the registered external language law.
